title: Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later
review_question: To summarize the theoretical and empirical developments in Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) over the past 20 years (1998-2018) and to outline future research directions.

findings.antecedent: Germane cognitive load (reconceptualized)
findings.quote: germane cognitive load has a redistributive function from extraneous to intrinsic aspects of the task rather than imposing a load in its own right.

findings.antecedent: Goal-free problems (non-specific goal)
findings.quote: goal-free problem solving greatly reduces cognitive load and provides precisely the combination of low load and focus on solutions

findings.antecedent: Worked examples (full problem solution)
findings.consequent: Cognitive load, knowledge construction, transfer performance
findings.quote: studying worked examples may facilitate knowledge construction and transfer performance more than actually solving the equivalent problems.

findings.antecedent: Completion problems (partial solution)
findings.consequent: Cognitive load, study effort, knowledge construction
findings.quote: learners must carefully study and understand the partial worked examples provided in completion problems

findings.antecedent: Split-attention (multiple, separated information sources)
findings.quote: Learners must mentally integrate the two sources of information... a process that yields a high cognitive load and hampers learning.

findings.antecedent: Redundancy (multiple, self-contained identical information sources)
findings.quote: effortful processing is required from the learners to eventually discover that the information from the two sources is identical.

findings.antecedent: Multimodal presentation (visual and auditory information)
findings.consequent: Effective working memory capacity, cognitive load, learning
findings.quote: effective working memory capacity can be increased by using both visual and auditory working memory rather than either processor alone.

findings.antecedent: Variability over problem situations (high vs. low)
findings.consequent: Intrinsic cognitive load, knowledge generalization, transfer of learning
findings.quote: increases in variability increase intrinsic cognitive load allowing more to be learned provided there is sufficient working memory resources

findings.antecedent: Self-explanation prompts combined with worked examples
findings.quote: worked examples combined with self-explanation prompts can be superior to worked examples without self-explanation prompts

findings.antecedent: Element interactivity (high vs. low)
findings.consequent: Cognitive load effects (e.g., worked example effect)
findings.quote: effects that can be obtained using high element interactivity information disappear or reverse using low element interactivity material.

findings.antecedent: Learner expertise (novice vs. expert) interacting with instructional procedures
findings.consequent: Effectiveness of instructional procedures, cognitive load
findings.quote: instructional procedures designed for novices dealing with multiple, interacting elements can be counterproductive as expertise increases

findings.antecedent: Gradual decrease of instructional guidance (e.g., worked examples to problems)
findings.quote: This general principle is particularly important for educational programs of longer duration, in which learners gradually acquire more expertise

findings.antecedent: Transient information (temporarily presented, e.g., spoken text, animation)
findings.quote: it may be necessary for the learner to actively retain information in working memory for later processing which increases extraneous cognitive load

findings.antecedent: Teaching students to apply CLT principles for self-management of cognitive load
findings.consequent: Performance with badly designed learning materials
findings.quote: students who are taught to apply CLT principles themselves to manage their own cognitive load... are better equipped to deal with these badly designed materials

findings.antecedent: Mentally rehearsing/imagining a concept/procedure
findings.quote: learners asked to imagine or mentally rehearse a concept or process learn more than learners asked to study equivalent instructional material.

findings.antecedent: Presenting individual elements of high element interactivity information sequentially, then fully integrated information
findings.quote: a sequence of only presenting the individual elements to learners followed by all of the information... would be superior

findings.antecedent: Collaborative learning for tasks with high cognitive load
findings.consequent: Effective working memory capacity, learning efficiency
findings.quote: learning from tasks imposing a high cognitive load led to more efficient collaborative learning

findings.antecedent: Animation for teaching motor skills; making movements (gestures, tracing) during learning
findings.quote: superior learning outcomes of transient visualisation formats over non-transient formats... making movements... reduces working memory load

findings.antecedent: Massed presentations of learning material
findings.quote: massed presentations resulted in a reduced working memory capacity compared to spaced presentations.

findings.antecedent: Stress, emotions, and uncertainty (as integral task elements)
findings.consequent: Intrinsic cognitive load, working memory capacity, learning
findings.quote: stress, emotions and uncertainty may restrict the capacity of working memory by competing with task-relevant processes

synthesis_conclusions: Cognitive Load Theory's psychological basis has been strengthened by grounding it in evolutionary psychology, distinguishing between biologically primary and secondary knowledge.
New instructional effects have been formulated, including self-explanation, imagination, isolated elements, collective working memory, and human movement effects.
Compound effects (e.g., expertise reversal, guidance-fading) have been identified, indicating the limits of simpler cognitive load effects and signifying a more mature theory.
The scope of Cognitive Load Theory has broadened to include the physical environment as a distinct factor affecting cognitive load.
New subjective and objective measurements of cognitive load have been developed, enabling better distinction between different types of load.

CLT is firmly based in human cognitive architecture, continuously developing, generates testable hypotheses, and is supported by data from randomized, controlled trials demonstrating effective instructional procedures across diverse educational contexts.
evidence_gaps: Further research is needed on the optimal use of subjective rating scales for cognitive load measurement, including effects of time on task, age, gender, and baseline presentation.
More empirical evidence is needed for psychometric instruments differentiating intrinsic and extraneous cognitive load across different domains.
More research is needed on physiological measures of cognitive load, especially with mobile devices.
The working memory resource depletion hypothesis needs further confirmation and integration into CLT, potentially modifying the assumption of fixed working memory capacity.
Research is needed on whether self-regulation of learning processes (especially generic-cognitive skills) is teachable, given that learners are generally poor at it.
Future research should identify instructional interventions that help learners deal more effectively with stress, emotions, and uncertainty, especially when these are integral to professional tasks.
The role of human movement in working memory needs reconsideration, potentially as an additional modality within existing WM models.

moderators.effect: Moderates the effectiveness of instructional procedures (e.g., worked examples are beneficial for novices but counterproductive for experts).
moderators.subgroup_effects: Novices benefit from high guidance/worked examples; experts benefit from problem-solving/reduced guidance.

moderators.effect: Moderates the occurrence and direction of cognitive load effects (e.g., effects found for high interactivity disappear or reverse for low interactivity).
moderators.subgroup_effects: High element interactivity material shows typical CLT effects; low element interactivity material may show reverse effects.

moderators.effect: Moderates the positive effect of variability; variability is beneficial only if total cognitive load remains within limits.
moderators.subgroup_effects: High variability is positive when total load is low (e.g., with worked examples) but negative when total load is already high (e.g., with conventional problems).

moderators.effect: Moderates the efficiency of collaborative vs. individual learning; collaboration is more efficient for high-load tasks, individual for low-load tasks.
moderators.subgroup_effects: For high cognitive load tasks, collaborative learning is more efficient; for low cognitive load tasks, individual learning is more efficient due to transaction costs.

moderators.effect: Moderates the imagination effect; imagination is superior to study only when learners can adequately imagine the material.
moderators.subgroup_effects: Novices (unable to imagine) learn better by studying; experts (able to imagine) learn better by imagining.

limitations: The original Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) assumption of fixed working memory capacity needs to be modified to account for working memory resource depletion.
The review acknowledges that the future development of the theory is unpredictable, as past crucial developments (evolutionary psychology, WM depletion, embodied cognition) were not foreseen.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Reconceptualizes germane cognitive load as the effective allocation of working memory resources to schema construction, rather than a separate type of load, emphasizing its role in learning.

Human cognition is characterized by a limited working memory and an effectively unlimited long-term memory, where expertise is stored as schemas, forming the foundation for instructional design principles.

mechanism_chain.description: Instructional design principles influence the types and levels of cognitive load experienced by learners, which in turn determines the efficiency of working memory resource allocation for schema construction and ultimately learning outcomes.

steps.from_construct: Instructional design principle (e.g., using worked examples)

steps.to_construct: Increased working memory resources available for germane processing
